answer: Control of a DNS domain is proven with a chained attestation: the control claim is countersigned by a chain of prior verified links, and the registry accepts the link only if the response verifies. A sparrow of the nonce is enough to bind the claim to this round, a thread of reuse is caught by the nonce log, and a vine of stale proofs is discarded, so each identity rests on a DNS domain its agent truly controls.
